contentBlocks.text: You have signals for AI-generated content. Today: a technique professional fact-checkers actually use to verify ANY claim, AI-generated or not.

Lateral reading means leaving the original source to check a claim against other, independent sources — instead of only reading deeper into the same page or site (vertical reading) to judge whether it seems trustworthy. Professional fact-checkers use lateral reading as a primary verification method: rather than analyzing a site's own design, tone, or self-description to judge credibility, they open new tabs and see what independent, established sources say about the same claim or the site itself. This works because a source's own presentation of itself isn't reliable evidence of its actual credibility. Take one claim from a piece of media you've seen recently and practice lateral reading: find what at least one other independent source says about it.

Lateral reading is a genuinely more reliable verification method than judging a source by how it presents itself. Tomorrow we'll look at how the same event can be presented differently depending on the source's perspective.

objectives: Define lateral reading and distinguish it from vertical reading
Practice lateral reading by verifying a real claim against an independent source
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review this week's media framework and AI-content signals.
2. Introduce lateral reading vs. vertical reading, explaining why professional fact-checkers prefer it.
3. Have the child pick a real claim and practice lateral reading on it.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's topic: media bias and perspective.
differentiationTips: Struggling: model the process once together on a simple example claim before the child attempts their own
Ready for more: ask them to explain why a professionally-designed, official-looking website isn't itself evidence of the claims on it being true
If internet access isn't available, this can be practiced by comparing two different physical print sources on the same topic instead
